clue.text: H's work at vice removal is affecting the brain

indicators.note: a removal shifts things from where they were, so the letters before it are moved into a new order

blocks.note: H is Hitchcock, the preamble's master of suspense, and Psycho is his 1960 film
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A film about cleaning up vice turns out to mess with your head.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle H is Alfred Hitchcock, the 'big suspender' of the preamble, a pun on master of suspense; 'H's work' is one of his films.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoactive drugs are those that act on the mind, altering mood, perception or behaviour.

clue.text: Royal resort between rivers in compound

indicators.note: to sit between two things is to have one on each side, so the rivers flank the resort

blocks.note: two rivers: the Po in Italy and R, the standard abbreviation for river
Lyme Regis is a Dorset seaside town; Regis is Latin for of the king, hence royal

explanation.surface: A royal holiday town lies between two rivers inside some walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort is Lyme Regis on England's south coast; dropping the Regis is the joke, because 'Royal' has done its work.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymer is a chemical compound built from many repeated molecular units.

clue.text: Make over for heartless solvers, very quietly if you begin

indicators.note: a thing without its heart has lost its central part, so the middle letter of solvers' word goes
where a word begins is its opening letter, so only that one is wanted

blocks.note: the setter addresses the solvers as you
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
taken as written
the opening letter of you

explanation.surface: A setter offers a makeover to heartless solvers if they just start quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: To yuppify a place or person is to remake it in the style of young urban professionals, a gentrifying makeover.

clue.text: Comforter in bed, consumption much exaggerated in space

indicators.note: to be in a space is to be enclosed by it, so the first two pieces sit inside it

blocks.note: consumption is the old name for tuberculosis, abbreviated TB
over the top, abbreviated OTT
a hole is an empty space

explanation.surface: A bedridden invalid's illness is wildly overstated by some cosmic observer.
explanation.walkthrough: Consumption here is the disease, not eating; TB is tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot bottle, usually a hot-water bottle, is placed between the sheets to warm and comfort a sleeper.

clue.text: Backwater for Irish and Norse gods

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end towards the start

blocks.note: the water part is the sea, a body of water, and the word's opening tells you to read it backwards
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A sleepy backwater serves as home to the Irish and the old Norse gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backwater' looks like one word meaning a quiet place; split it into an instruction and a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aesir are the principal tribe of deities in Norse mythology, including Odin, Thor and Frigg.

clue.text: Singular work of H getting hissed off stage

definitions.note: the answer is what a performer gets: to get the bird is to be hissed off

blocks.note: first meaning: Hitchcock's film ... made singular
second meaning: theatre slang for being hissed or booed by the audience

explanation.surface: An actor in a Hitchcock production is booed off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' is a British theatre idiom for being hissed at, from the hissing of geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping the plural from the film title leaves the phrase for an audience's hissing and jeering.

clue.text: H's work naturally makes me turn green

definitions.note: describes what the answer does rather than naming it

blocks.note: first meaning: Hitchcock's 1958 film
second meaning: the giddy spinning that leaves a sufferer nauseous; vert is also heraldic green

explanation.surface: Watching a Hitchcock film leaves me feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin root means a whirling, so it makes me turn; green is both nauseous and vert, which begins the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is the dizzy sensation of spinning, often bringing on nausea, the green-faced look of sickness.

clue.text: 'Oly H, enemy of fashion, doesn't lose 9, they say

blocks.note: holy with its aitch dropped; a holy person is a saint, ST
H is Hitch, Hitchcock's nickname, said the same aitch-dropping way
in means fashionable
time is the old enemy, as in the phrase time, the enemy

explanation.surface: A Cockney-sounding saint called Hitch, scornful of fashion, refuses to give up nine of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Oly tells you to drop the aitch, and the same treatment turns Hitch into a scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a stitch in time saves nine: a small timely repair avoids nine later, so nine are not lost.

clue.text: Small child holding a speaker wins the palm

indicators.note: something holding another clasps it inside, so the child surrounds what follows

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written
the lip, an organ of speech; lip is also cheeky talk

explanation.surface: A toddler clutching a loudspeaker carries off the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wins the palm' sounds like taking the prize, the palm being a victor's emblem; here the palm is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The talipot is a tall fan palm of southern India and Sri Lanka, famous for its huge leaves.

clue.text: Holy person deserves to precede Eliot, the poet

definitions.note: names the poet's middle name: the word that comes just before Eliot

blocks.note: a saint, abbreviated ST
to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: A saintly figure has earned the right to stand ahead of the poet Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the name that comes just before Eliot in Thomas Stearns Eliot, the poet T. S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot's full name is Thomas Stearns Eliot, so his middle name comes right before the surname.

clue.text: H's work for arrogant interns, as composed

indicators.note: a composed piece is put together from parts, so these letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: all seventeen letters of these three words are the material

explanation.surface: A Hitchcock film is recommended viewing for cocky junior doctors, as made up.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangers on a Train is Hitchcock's 1951 thriller, a film and therefore a work by him.

clue.text: Morning on film, going into Mexican port

indicators.note: going into something means entering it and ending up enclosed

blocks.note: a.m., before noon
a pic is a film or picture
into supplies its shorter form to, meaning towards

explanation.surface: A morning spent filming in a Mexican harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the morning before the film; the whole pair then sits inside the two letters to.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampico is a major seaport on Mexico's Gulf coast, in the state of Tamaulipas.

clue.text: Grace in films became increasingly wet

definitions.note: names the prince whose wife Grace became, not a verb

blocks.note: first meaning: Grace Kelly, star of three Hitchcock films
second meaning: comparative of rainy

explanation.surface: An actress in a film grows ever soggier.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace Kelly starred in Dial M for Murder, Rear Window and To Catch a Thief before marrying Monaco's ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace Kelly married Prince Rainier III and became Princess of Monaco; rainier also means more rainy.

clue.text: Pester the prince

blocks.note: first meaning: to harass or worry persistently
second meaning: Prince ..., younger son of King Charles

explanation.surface: Paparazzi hound a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry also fills 19 down's Hitchcock title, The Trouble with Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass repeatedly; Harry is also the familiar name of a British royal.

clue.text: Moderated and went on changing, keeping back eccentric

indicators.note: things changing take a new form, so the letters of the words before it are reordered
back means read from right to left
to keep something is to hold it inside, so the reworked letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
odd means eccentric

explanation.surface: Someone moderated their behaviour, carrying on changing while holding an oddball back.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned down means made less extreme or intense, softened in force or tone.

clue.text: Some note or notes on H's work

indicators.note: only some of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written
IOUs are notes promising repayment of a debt

explanation.surface: Someone jots a few notes on a Hitchcock film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like music or memos, but here it is promissory notes, IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious is Hitchcock's 1946 spy thriller starring Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman, one of his films.

clue.text: H's direction, its first part having got by

indicators.note: the opening part has gone past and is no longer there, with by itself part of what goes

blocks.note: Hitchcock's 1959 film North by Northwest, his direction in both senses

explanation.surface: A film director's chosen heading, the early stretch already behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' is the film he directed and the compass heading; 'got by' is a pun, since the title's first part, North by, gets cut.
explanation.definitionFit: North-west is the compass point midway between north and west, a heading or bearing.

clue.text: H's 23 girl

definitions.note: 23 across is a cross-reference, so this reads as the riotous girl

blocks.note: first meaning: Hitchcock's 1940 film, his first in Hollywood
second meaning: the girl of the ... Riots, Welsh rural protests of 1839-43

explanation.walkthrough: 23 across gives a word meaning unruly; the Rebecca Riots were Welsh toll-gate protests whose leaders dressed as women and called themselves Rebecca.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a Hitchcock film from du Maurier's novel and the female name adopted by Welsh rioters.

clue.text: Parasitic worm, caddish type, holding its breath?

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so the cad's word wraps round the breath

blocks.note: a heel is a cad, a dishonourable man
breath is air drawn into the lungs

explanation.surface: A worm-like scoundrel holds its breath, perhaps to avoid detection.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks whether a worm can hold its breath; that whimsy is the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair-eel is an old name for the horsehair worm, a long thin nematode-like creature parasitic in insects.

clue.text: Do business with the wind

definitions.note: a noun naming the trade wind

blocks.note: first meaning: to buy and sell
second meaning: the ..., short for the ... winds that blow steadily towards the equator

explanation.surface: A sailing merchant trades by catching the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to buy and sell goods; the trades are steady tropical easterly winds once used by merchant sailing ships.

clue.text: Time and money with 13 is H's work

definitions.note: the answer plus with 13 down's Harry makes the film title

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: Time and money spent on a prince turn into a Hitchcock production.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is the prince Harry, so the film is The Trouble with Harry (1955), a dark comedy about a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock directed The Trouble with Harry, so this word followed by with Harry completes his film title.

clue.text: Enraged maybe by diabolical road use

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist is driven to fury by terrible driving on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks enraged as one example of being stirred up; anger is one kind of arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroused means stirred to strong feeling, and anger is one such feeling, hence the hedge.

clue.text: One pound unit may be integral to the structure

explanation.definitionFit: In-built describes a feature built in as an inherent, fixed part of something rather than added.

taken as written
the United States

taken as written

clue.text: Roy, the golden beast of the prairie

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
the American bison roams the prairies

clue.text: Deceleration depends on gravity and air resistance

definitions.text: depends on gravity and air resistance
definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it

blocks.note: first meaning: speed that is falling, slowing down

blocks.clueFragment: depends on gravity and air resistance
blocks.note: second meaning: the velocity of a dropping body, set by pull and drag

explanation.surface: A physics statement: how fast something slows depends on gravity and drag.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one physics fact; split it, and falling is first an adjective on speed, then a verb for dropping.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed that is falling is slowing down; a falling object's velocity is governed by gravitational pull and drag.
